entries.source: Adolph Friedrich Riedel, Codex diplomaticus Brandenburgensis, series B, volume II, p. 140; series A, volume XXIV
entries.summary: Margrave Ludwig takes the von Rosenberg and von Bredow families, with Plate Castle, under his protection, 17 October 1338.
entries.latin: Nouerint etc. Quod nos Ludouicus etc. recepimus in nostram familiam ac tuitionem presentibus recipimus fratrem Johannem de Rosenberg, wernherum et werenherum de Rosenberg, fratres, nec non Petrum militem, copkinum, willekinum et matheum fratres dictos de Bredowe cum castro Plate et aliis suis municionibus, quos habent pro nunc et habere possunt in futurum, volentes ipsos contra quemlibet tueri et in suo jure defensare: et in adjutorium esse debemus et de suis juribus habere plenum posse. Debent enim ipsi suas municiones predictas contra quemlibet presentare et omnimode nobis aperire. Et cum nos vel quicunque nostri nomine statuerimus, ipsas municiones intrauerimus, extunc expensas in omnibus tenere debemus et largire. Et si capitaneus noster equitare vel aliquid aliud facere jusserit et in hoc dampna perceperint, illa ipsis equimilibus refundemus. Et si, quod absit, suas municiones in nostro servicio perdiderint, secundum consilium duorum nostrorum fidelium vasallorum et duorum suorum amicorum indemnes tenere volumus et ipsis aliis bonis recompensos. Si eciam per edificia vel alium modum circumvallati et obessi fuerint, ipsos in quatuor ebdomadarum spacio de ipsa obsessione redimemus. Et si aliquas gweras habuerint et aliqui de nostris fidelibus vel de suis amicis ipsos juvare voluerint, hi de nostro consensu fore debent et beneplacito voluntatis. Et si domino Episcopo Magdeburgensi vel aliquibus suis amicis nostri nomine diffidationem jusserimus, tunc ipsis tantum dare temporis spacium debemus, sicut domino Jo. de Buch, capitaneo nostro dilecto, videbitur convenire, quod in suo honore se servare possent. Et cum aliquis rixas nostri nomine habuerint, ex tunc ipsis in bonis inimicorum dare debemus lucrum bonorum recompensam, sicut domino Jo. de Buch memorato videbitur conform racioni. Huius rei Testes Dominus Jo. de Buch sepedictus, Henricus ysoldsrider, Rutenie, milites, Gerko wolff cum ceteris. Ut singula premissa etc. Datum Berlin, anno domini Millesimo CCCo. XXXo. VIIIo. in vigilia Luce Evangeliste.
entries.english: Know all, etc. Whereas we, Ludwig, etc., have received into our household and protection, by this present instrument we receive Lord Johann von Rosenberg, Wernher and Werenher von Rosenberg, brothers, and also Peter, a knight, Copkin, Willekin, and Matheus, brothers, called von Bredow, together with Plate Castle and their other fortifications, which they now possess and may possess in the future, wishing to protect them against everyone and defend them in their rights. We are bound to assist them and to give them full power to exercise their rights. For they must present the aforesaid fortifications to us against anyone and disclose them to us in every respect. Whenever we, or anyone acting in our name, decide to enter those fortifications, from then on we must provide and pay all expenses. If our captain orders them to ride out or do anything else, and they suffer losses in doing so, we will repay those losses to them in full. If, God forbid, they lose their fortifications in our service, we wish to hold them harmless, on the advice of two of our faithful vassals and two of their friends, and to compensate them with other goods. If they are surrounded and besieged by siege works or by any other means, we will ransom them from that siege within four weeks. If they are involved in any wars and some of our faithful men or their friends wish to help them, those men must do so with our consent and at our pleasure. If we, in our name, order a challenge to the Bishop of Magdeburg or any of his friends, then we must grant them such a period of time as our beloved captain, Lord Johann von Buch, considers appropriate, so that they may preserve their honor. If anyone becomes involved in a quarrel on our behalf, we must then grant them compensation from the goods of their enemies, as the aforesaid Lord Johann von Buch considers just. Witnesses to this matter: the aforesaid Lord Johann von Buch, Henricus Ysoldsrider, Rutenie, knights, Gerko Wolff, and others. So that all the foregoing may be observed, etc. Given at Berlin in the year of our Lord 1338, on the eve of Saint Luke the Evangelist.
